title: Multiplying 9 × 11 by 11 × 11 matrices with 708 multiplications
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that the matrix multiplication tensor ⟨9, 11, 11⟩ has rank at most 708 over the rationals. Two compared theorems: 708 triples of rational matrices decompose the tensor (∑ᵢ uᵢ[a, b] vᵢ[c, d] wᵢ[e, f] = [b = c ∧ a = e ∧ d = f]), and the same triples form a bilinear algorithm A * B = ∑ᵢ (∑ uᵢ[a, b] A[a, b]) (∑ vᵢ[c, d] B[c, d]) wᵢ over every field of characteristic zero. The scheme, scaled to integers, is data; Lean's kernel checks it (decide +kernel, no native_decide) slice by slice with the coefficients packed into large integers, and a soundness proof for every input turns the 99 slice checks, a range check and a bound check into the tensor identity. The smallest rank listed for this format in the Lille catalogue was 710 when this was written.
